overview: A pantheon is the first belief, bought with the first twenty-five Faith and held for the whole game. One per civilization, chosen from a list that empties as rivals pick. It affects only your own cities and never leaves them, which is why the right pantheon is the one that matches the ground you settled, not the one that sounds strongest.

pantheons.name: City Patron Goddess
pantheons.effect: +25% Production toward districts in cities without a specialty district.
pantheons.note: Every new city builds its first district faster; strongest for wide, fast-settling empires.

pantheons.name: Dance of the Aurora
pantheons.effect: Holy Site districts get +1 Faith for each adjacent Tundra tile.
pantheons.note: Russia's pantheon in all but name: the Lavra stacks it on top of its own tundra bonus.

pantheons.name: Desert Folklore
pantheons.effect: Holy Site districts get +1 Faith for each adjacent Desert tile.
pantheons.note: Turns a desert start into a faith start. Combine with Petra for the best desert city in the game.

pantheons.name: Divine Spark
pantheons.effect: +1 Great Person point from Holy Sites (Prophet), Campuses with a Library (Scientist) and Theater Squares with an Amphitheater (Writer).
pantheons.note: A quiet pantheon that compounds; pick it when the land offers nothing to exploit.

pantheons.name: Earth Goddess
pantheons.effect: +1 Faith from tiles with Breathtaking Appeal.
pantheons.note: Strong wherever mountains, coast and woods raise appeal; weak in flat farmland.

pantheons.name: Fertility Rites
pantheons.effect: City growth rate +10%, and a free Builder in the city that founded the pantheon.
pantheons.note: The free Builder is worth more than the growth. A default when nothing else fits.

pantheons.name: Fire Goddess
pantheons.effect: +2 Faith from Geothermal Fissures and Volcanic Soil (Gathering Storm).
pantheons.note: Only worth it with two or more fissures or volcanoes in reach of the capital.

pantheons.name: God of Craftsmen
pantheons.effect: +1 Production from improved Strategic resources.
pantheons.note: Horses, Iron and Niter mines all count; a cavalry civilization with Horses in the capital takes it.

pantheons.name: God of Healing
pantheons.effect: +30 healing for units adjacent to a Holy Site.
pantheons.note: A defensive pantheon for a faith civilization; the Holy Site becomes a field hospital.

pantheons.name: God of the Forge
pantheons.effect: +25% Production toward Ancient and Classical era military units.
pantheons.note: The Spike pantheon: faster War-Carts, faster Hypaspists, faster everything the window needs.

pantheons.name: God of the Open Sky
pantheons.effect: +1 Culture from Pastures.
pantheons.note: Scythia and Mongolia start among horses and sheep; the pastures pay civics from turn ten.

pantheons.name: God of the Sea
pantheons.effect: +1 Production from Fishing Boats.
pantheons.note: Coastal cities with four or more sea resources build like inland ones. The Māori take it by reflex.

pantheons.name: God of War
pantheons.effect: Bonus Faith equal to 50% of the Combat Strength of each enemy unit killed within 8 tiles of a Holy Site.
pantheons.note: A war of religion pays twice. Build the Holy Site on the border the war will cross.

pantheons.name: Goddess of Festivals
pantheons.effect: +1 Culture from Plantations.
pantheons.note: Bananas, cocoa, sugar, silk, dyes, spices: a rainforest start with plantations is a culture start.

pantheons.name: Goddess of the Harvest
pantheons.effect: Harvesting a resource or removing a feature grants Faith equal to the yield gained.
pantheons.note: Chop a forest, bank the faith. Strong with Magnus and extra Builder charges.

pantheons.name: Goddess of the Hunt
pantheons.effect: +1 Food and +1 Production from Camps.
pantheons.note: Furs, deer, truffles and ivory; a northern start with three camps grows on it.

pantheons.name: Initiation Rites
pantheons.effect: +50 Faith for each Barbarian Outpost cleared, and the unit that clears it heals fully.
pantheons.note: For leaders who were going to clear the camps anyway. Expires with the camps.

pantheons.name: Lady of the Reeds and Marshes
pantheons.effect: +2 Production from Marsh, Oasis and Desert Floodplains.
pantheons.note: A Nile start with floodplains on both banks builds wonders on this alone.

pantheons.name: Monument to the Gods
pantheons.effect: +15% Production toward Ancient and Classical era wonders.
pantheons.note: The wonder-rusher's pantheon; it stops paying after the Classical era.

pantheons.name: Oral Tradition
pantheons.effect: +1 Culture from Plantations (Gathering Storm: from Bananas, Citrus, Cotton, Dyes, Silk, Spices and Sugar plantations).
pantheons.note: Overlaps with Goddess of Festivals by expansion; take whichever your version offers for your resources.

pantheons.name: Religious Idols
pantheons.effect: +2 Faith from Mines over Luxury and Bonus resources.
pantheons.note: Hills full of silver, gems and copper become a faith economy without a Holy Site.

pantheons.name: Religious Settlements
pantheons.effect: Border expansion rate +15%, and a free Settler in the city that founded the pantheon.
pantheons.note: A free Settler is a free city. Taken first in most multiplayer games; take it if it is still there.

pantheons.name: River Goddess
pantheons.effect: +2 Amenities and +2 Housing to cities whose Holy Site is adjacent to a river.
pantheons.note: Two amenities per city is a whole Entertainment Complex; plan every Holy Site on a river bank.

pantheons.name: Sacred Path
pantheons.effect: Holy Site districts get +1 Faith for each adjacent Rainforest tile.
pantheons.note: The Khmer pantheon: rainforest Holy Sites stack with the Prasat.

pantheons.name: Stone Circles
pantheons.effect: +2 Faith from Quarries.
pantheons.note: Stone, marble and gypsum in the capital's ring make this the fastest road to a religion.
